timeline_empty: Nothing has happened since the server started
banner_offline: Disconnected. Gave up after {tries} tries; it reconnects when you return to this tab.
banner_replaced: This address does not work here (the sb server may have restarted, or the link expired): on this computer open /boss gui; on a phone scan a new QR code.
banner_reconnecting: Disconnected from the straw net. Reconnecting… The view shows the last known state.
banner_reconnecting_try: Disconnected from the straw net. Reconnecting (try {attempt})… The view shows the last known state.
banner_problem: The server is up but cannot read the net: {problem}
problem_snapshot: the server sent a snapshot the page cannot read
problem_unknown: the server reported a problem the page cannot read
lost_workspace: This workspace is not part of the net.
docs_cut: More than the relay carries: read them in the terminal.
note_unknown: Not in the net (it may have ended more than ten minutes ago).
note_recent: No longer live; its history stays readable for ten minutes.
unreachable: The server could not be reached.
unsure: Not confirmed. Check the terminal before sending again.
went: The original already went to the session; what is here is your edited copy, unsent.
sent_edited: Sent as it was; your edits stayed here, unsent.
blocked_offline: The stream is down; sending waits for it to come back.
blocked_ended: This session is no longer live; its history stays readable.
blocked_no_pane: No live pi pane backs this unit, so there is nothing to type into.
blocked_agent: This is a {agent} session. It is in the net, but this page cannot type into it or show its log: use its own terminal.
blocked_answer_above: It waits on a dialog: answer it above, or in its terminal.
blocked_answer_terminal: It waits on a dialog; answer it in its terminal.
too_long: The text is longer than 16 KB; shorten it.
ends_session: {command} ends this session or switches its pane to another one.
stop_ask: Stop the current task? Queued messages go back to its terminal editor.
ask_own_words: It also takes your own words.
refused_digest: The question changed; read it again.
refused_not_allowed: That answer does not fit the question.
refused_malformed: The session could not read that answer.
stale_local: It was already answered in the terminal.
stale_cancel: It was dismissed in the terminal.
answer_busy: Another answer is on its way; check the terminal.
has_preview: It has a preview; see it in the terminal.
secret_remote: For security, entering a secret is not supported remotely. Answer it in the terminal on the computer the GUI runs on.
secret_terminal: A secret is entered in the terminal only, not here. Answer it in the terminal on the computer the GUI runs on.
opened_during: Opened while {tool} was running; it may not be about that call.
other_answer: The other answer was not taken; this one can go.
retry_terminal: {why} Open the terminal again to retry.
paused_hidden: Paused while this tab is hidden.
mirror_hidden: Hidden while it waits for a secret; type it in the terminal.
doc_gone: Unavailable: no longer open in its session.
doc_unlisted: No longer listed: closed in its session, or the session ended.
doc_updated: Updated: the new version loads when this tile shows.
server_title: The sb server: state, restart, and log
server_restart_confirm: Restart the sb server? This page keeps its address and reconnects by itself. Runs and dialogs carry on.
server_restarted: Restarting. This page reconnects when the server is back; if it does not, open /boss gui (the address changes when a port was taken).
pair_scan: Scan it with a phone signed in to Tailscale as this machine's user. It works once, within ten minutes.
pair_code: Or, in an installed app, type these 8 characters (no hyphen needed). It works once, within ten minutes.
remote_off_ask: Remote access is off. Turn it on so a phone on your tailnet can open this page? Only devices signed in to Tailscale as this machine's user can pair; Funnel is never used.
opened_main: The main is open in a new squad of {base}.
opened_base: The base is open with its first member.
close_base_ask: Quit base {name}? Every agent in it and its tower quit. Nothing quits while anything running would be lost.
close_squad_ask: Quit squad {name}? Every agent in it quits.
close_unit_ask: Quit {name}? It quits pi and its pane closes.
close_tower_ask: Quit the tower {name}? The base's mains become members again.
edit_taken: The queued messages are in the box. Edit them and send.
edit_none: Nothing is queued any more: the messages were delivered, or they are in the terminal’s editor.
edit_unsure: Not confirmed. If the messages were taken back, fetch them again; otherwise they are still in the terminal.
take_no_key: pi’s dequeue key (app.message.dequeue in its keybindings.json) is not one this page can send. Press it in the terminal.
take_no_editor: This session has no editor to take the messages back into.
take_stale: The take-back timed out, or the session changed, after the key went: the messages are in the terminal’s editor, not here.
take_not_taken: pi did not take its queue back; its dequeue key may not be {key}. Check the terminal.
take_changed: The terminal’s editor holds something other than the queued messages and the draft (typed meanwhile, or a message pi expanded). The messages are in it; check the terminal.
take_too_large: The queued messages are too long to bring here. They are in the terminal’s editor.
take_not_cleared: The messages could not be cleared from the terminal’s editor. They are there, not here.
take_blocked: It is waiting on a dialog: answer it in the terminal.
take_local_only: While it waits on a link request, a paired device can only send Escape. Approve it on this computer’s own page or terminal.
take_rate: Too many keys at once. Try again in a second.
take_busy: Another input to this session is still on its way.
remind_on: Reminders on: while the page is in the background, a unit waiting on you, finishing, or failing raises a system notification
remind_blocked: The browser blocks notifications; allow them in the site settings
sound_title: Sounds: on or off, volume, and a try
finished_title: Notices: units that finished or failed. A row opens its comms and clears it, or clear them all
typing_direct: ◉ Keyboard goes to the pane · click outside to stop
typing_hint: Click here and the keyboard goes straight to the terminal (except Ctrl, Alt, and ⌘ combinations)
stash_base_ask: Stash base {name}? Its tower, mains, and members quit and come back with Pop. Nothing is stashed while anything running would be lost.
remote_stays: Turning remote access off keeps the paired devices. Unpair a device to end its pairing.
deploy_timeout: No answer after {seconds} s. The unit may still open; check the map.
deploy_trust: Waiting for your OK to trust this folder
deploy_settings_special: Not started: {path} is not a plain file (a device, pipe or socket, or a link to one). pi reads it whole when it starts and could hang. Make it a plain file or remove it, then try again.
deploy_settings_large: Not started: {path} is over the {limit} KB limit. pi reads it whole when it starts. Make it smaller or remove it, then try again.
deploy_settings_unreadable: Not started: {path} cannot be read{code}. Fix it or remove it, then try again.
deploy_settings_unchecked: Not started: {path} could not be checked in time{code}. pi reads it whole when it starts. Try again, or make it a plain file or remove it.
trust_body: Trusting lets the agent load this folder's settings, extensions, skills, prompts, themes, and MCP servers, and install the packages its settings name. Extensions and MCP servers run as programs on this computer. Don't trust a folder you don't know the origin of.
trust_terminal: The agent's terminal can answer too; the first answer counts.
trust_gone: The agent ended before the answer arrived; nothing was decided.
trust_folder_changed: The folder changed after the question was shown, so your answer was not used. Read the new question and answer again.
trust_changed: The question changed or is closed; read it again.
trust_reminder: An agent needs your OK to load a folder's settings
link_a_join_unattended: {label} ({short}), an unattended device, asks to join team {team}
link_a_confirm: {label} ({short}) asks you to confirm a {tool} call from its tower {tower}, which acts on a message you sent
link_a_mismatch: {label} ({short}) shows another roster than this computer in team {team}; the relay may be showing different rosters
link_a_unreachable: The relay of team {team} has been unreachable for {minutes} minutes

match.countPlural=one: {count} message waits in the inbox of team {team}: no tower is open on its project
match.countPlural=other: {count} messages wait in the inbox of team {team}: no tower is open on its project

match.countPlural=one: {count} message has waited more than 10 minutes for an idle tower in team {team}
match.countPlural=other: {count} messages have waited more than 10 minutes for an idle tower in team {team}

link_words_help: Look at {label}'s screen. Tap the set of four words it shows. A wrong tap ends the invite.
link_unattended_help: This device has no one at it. The id in your invite stands in for the words.
link_leave_only_admin_sure: Leave? You are the only admin: nobody can remove a device or rotate the key afterwards. Press again to leave anyway
link_second_admin: This computer is the team's only attended admin. If it is lost, nobody can remove a device or rotate the key. Make a second attended admin:
link_no_teams: No teams on this computer yet. Create one, or join with an invite.
link_share_status_long: Share my towers' and tabs' states
link_share_presence_long: Share only that I am online
link_invite_help: Scan it with the new computer's camera, or paste the text there. It works once. The new computer shows four words: tap the same set here.
link_copy_failed: Could not copy; the text is selected, copy it yourself
link_create_help: The relay's operator gives you a one-time team token. This computer becomes the team's first admin.
link_project_pick: Project folder (messages go to a tower open on it):
link_join_help: Paste the invite text, or scan its QR code. You are shown four words to read to the inviter, who taps the same set.
link_camera_failed: The camera could not be used: {reason}
link_join_waiting: Waiting for the inviter to confirm. The invite lapses in {time}.
link_join_waiting_pinned: Waiting for the inviter to approve this device.
link_join_need_project: You are added. Pick the project folder, then use it:
link_join_done: Joined. The team is under Teams.
link_setup_help: Straw Link has not started on this computer. Setting it up starts a link holder in one of its pi sessions (a tower or a joined session).
link_setup_wait: Starting. This takes a few seconds.
link_prefilled: An agent asked for this screen: {reason}
link_trust_help: What a message from this device may do. reply: the allowed read-only tools run; anything else asks you here. forward: the same, but anything else asks that device's owner on their computer. dispatch: runs as a message from you would, under this computer's own guards.
placeholder_event_run: Goes to the running event run · it answers here
conv_in_run: You are in event run {id} · started {time}
placeholder_conversation: Continues the boss conversation with the tower

match.countPlural=one: {count} Straw Link message has waited more than 10 minutes in the inbox of team {team} for an ally run. Look at the tower's card on the map: a held tower or a refused start keeps it waiting.
match.countPlural=other: {count} Straw Link messages have waited more than 10 minutes in the inbox of team {team} for an ally run. Look at the tower's card on the map: a held tower or a refused start keeps them waiting.

tower_notice_loop: Runs crashed or timed out again and again, so the tower stops waking. The queue is kept; Retry, or a message from the boss, wakes it again.
tower_notice_not_at_shell: The standing pane is not at its own shell: a nested shell or a program runs there. Leave it, then press Retry
tower_notice_unchecked: The tower could not check the standing pane for a program of yours, so it types nothing there; press Retry when it is free
tower_notice_nothing_typed: The tower types nothing in the standing pane: {reason}
tower_notice_late: An event was parked after two runs crashed with it: {what}
tower_err_standing: The tower is standing by: no run is live, so there is no terminal. Write to it in the composer; that wakes it.
tower_err_server_queue: These messages wait in the sb server's queue for the tower's next run; they are taken when it runs.
tower_err_no_tower: The sb server runs no tower for this workspace.
tower_term_standing: The tower is standing by, so it has no terminal. A run opens one when it wakes; write to it in Comms to wake it.
tower_term_held: The tower is held after repeated crashes, so it has no terminal. Retry it, or write to it in Comms.
placeholder_held: Held after repeated crashes · a message wakes it
boss_crash_flag: A run that crashed may already have handled this: check before acting.
ally_run_open: Read this ally run's comms (read only)
ally_run_unseen: Its comms are not shown yet: the run's session file is not known
event_run_state: a run the tower started for events · read only
tower_empty: This tower stands by. The sb server wakes it for a run when a message arrives; your first message here starts that run.
placeholder_ally: An ally run is answering a teammate · a message wakes a run of your own
blocked_run: The tower started this run for events. You can read its comms here; to talk to it, write to the tower.
blocked_ally: A teammate's message drives this ally run. You can read its comms here; you cannot write to it.
link_a_confirm_plain: {label} ({short}) asks you to confirm a {tool} call from its tower
ally_state: driven by a teammate's message · read only
memory_add_standing: A standing instruction, in your words
memory_rev: The memory changed since you read it, so it is shown again. Try once more.
memory_pending: Proposed by the tower, waiting for you
memory_proposal_add_standing: The tower proposes a standing instruction: {text}
memory_by_proposal: proposed by the tower, confirmed by you
conv_state_working: boss conversation · ends after {minutes} min idle
conv_state_waiting: boss conversation · waiting for you · ends after {minutes} min idle
conv_idle_deadline: waiting for you; it ends at {time} if you stay quiet
conv_working: working; it ends after {minutes} min idle
conv_leave_title: Ends the conversation with a note (the same as /boss tower leave). What it did not take waits for the next run.
conv_new_title: The next conversation starts a new session (the same as /boss tower new); a live one ends first.
conv_left: Leaving: the conversation ends with a note.
conv_fresh: Done: the next conversation is a new session.
conv_event_run_open: Open this event run's comms (read only)
conv_event_run_unseen: This event run's session is not known yet
lan_off_ask: Wi-Fi access is off. Turn it on so a phone on the same network as this computer can open this page? It answers only devices on this network's private addresses; each phone installs this computer's certificate once, and you allow each new device here.
lan_risk: Risk: anyone who copies this certificate's key from this computer (a backup, a program running as you, an agent you run) can pose to your phones, and to any computer that installed it, as {name}.local and as any private-network address, such as your router's or NAS's 192.168.x.x page, on any Wi-Fi they join, until you remove the certificate from each of them.
lan_risk_noname: Risk: anyone who copies this certificate's key from this computer (a backup, a program running as you, an agent you run) can pose to your phones, and to any computer that installed it, as any private-network address, such as your router's or NAS's 192.168.x.x page, on any Wi-Fi they join, until you remove the certificate from each of them.
lan_unverified: Not verified yet: whether your phone limits this certificate to this computer's name and private addresses has not been checked. Until it has, assume that a copy of the key could pose as any website to your phone. Use Tailscale instead if you can.
lan_hotspot: We recommend using Wi-Fi access on your phone's hotspot, or on a Wi-Fi that connects the phone directly to this computer, so no one else is on the network.
lan_risk_short: This computer's certificate is trusted by your phones. Whether they limit it has not been verified, so a copy of its key could pose as any website to them.
lan_turn_on: Make the certificate and turn on Wi-Fi access
lan_step_ca: Step 1, once per phone: give it this computer's certificate.
lan_share_ca: Download the certificate here, then send it to the phone by AirDrop or Quick Share (no check needed unless the phone asked you to accept it from an unknown sender).
lan_scan_ca: Or scan this on the phone, on a network you trust (a hotspot or direct Wi-Fi is best).
lan_fp_lead: If the phone downloaded it over Wi-Fi, check the fingerprint on the phone before trusting it. SHA-256 starts:
lan_fp_ios: iPhone, before Install: Profile Downloaded, the profile. Contains must say only Certificate; More Details must list exactly one certificate and nothing else, with this SHA-256. Otherwise tap Remove.
lan_fp_android: Android, after installing: Encryption & credentials, Trusted credentials, User must show exactly one Straw Boss LAN CA and nothing you did not add, with this SHA-256. Otherwise remove them now.
lan_fp_mac: Mac: Keychain Access, search Straw Boss: exactly one Straw Boss LAN CA, with this SHA-256 in Details.
lan_fp_windows: Windows: exactly one Security Warning appears, and its SHA-1 thumbprint is {sha1}. If a second warning appears, choose No, then remove the first in certmgr.msc.
lan_step_pair: Step 2: scan with the phone and tap Pair, then allow it here. The code works once, within ten minutes.
lan_show_code: Show a code for the installed app
lan_number_ask: Type the number your phone shows
lan_pending_many: More than one device used a code: only one of them can be your phone.
lan_pending_waiting: Pair request waiting from {peer}: run /boss gui lan
lan_vpn: A VPN carries this computer's traffic; if the phone cannot connect, allow local network access in the VPN's settings.
lan_refused: A Wi-Fi pairing code was used from {peer} and not allowed. If that was not your phone, someone saw the code.
lan_not_private: If the phone warns that the connection is not private, do not go on: install the certificate first (step 1).
lan_use_address: Use the address {address} instead of the name
lan_use_name: Use the name {name}.local instead of the address
lan_no_address: This computer has no private network address Wi-Fi access can serve now (a VPN tunnel is not served).
lan_ca_ending: This computer's Wi-Fi certificate ends on {date}. Run /boss gui lan reset in a pi session and choose renew; each phone installs the new one.
lan_ca_ended: This computer's Wi-Fi certificate has ended; run /boss gui lan reset in a pi session and choose renew, and each phone installs the new one.
lan_reset_hint: To make a new certificate, run /boss gui lan reset in a pi session.
lan_void: Too many wrong codes from {peers} addresses: this code is void. Choose Show a code for the installed app to get a new one (the QR still works). Someone on this network is guessing codes. Pair on your phone's hotspot instead.
lan_renamed_n: Another device on this network answers to {caName}.local, so macOS renamed this computer {name}. Use the address instead of the name below, and set the name back in System Settings, General, Sharing, Local hostname.
lan_renamed: This computer is now called {name}; the certificate is for {caName}.local. Run /boss gui lan reset in a pi session to make a new certificate (each phone installs it again).
lan_port_taken: Port {port} is taken on {address} by another program; Wi-Fi access does not serve that address. Run /boss gui lan in a pi session to move to a free port (installed apps then need to be added again).
lan_moved: Port {from} was taken on this computer; Wi-Fi access moved to {to}. An app installed from the old address needs adding again.
lan_stays_off_error: Wi-Fi access stays off: {message}. It is tried again when the server next starts.
lan_ca_corrupt: Wi-Fi access stays off: the certificate file is unreadable or readable by other accounts. Run /boss gui lan reset in a pi session to make a new certificate; each phone installs it again.
lan_ca_missing: Wi-Fi access stays off: this computer's Wi-Fi certificate is missing. Run /boss gui lan in a pi session to make a new one (each phone installs it again).
lan_secondary: Wi-Fi access is served by the default Herdr's sb server.
lan_ca_qr: QR code for the certificate page
lan_cant_open: If the phone cannot open it, use the address.
lan_wrong_budget: Three wrong numbers in a row, so every waiting request was denied. Press New code and pair again.
lan_share_profile: For iPhone or Mac: the profile (.mobileconfig)
lan_share_crt: For Android or Windows: the certificate (.crt)
lan_refused_n: A Wi-Fi pairing code was used from {peer} and not allowed, {count} times (last at {time}). If that was not your phone, someone saw the code.
lan_fw_block_all: The macOS firewall blocks all incoming connections, so a phone cannot connect: turn off "Block all incoming connections" in System Settings, Network, Firewall, Options.
lan_fw_block_node: The macOS firewall blocks node: allow it in System Settings, Network, Firewall, Options.
lan_fw_win_block_node: Windows Firewall has rules that block node.exe ({names}); they win over any allow rule.
lan_fw_win_block_port: Windows Firewall has rules that block TCP port {port} ({names}); they win over any allow rule.
lan_fw_win_block_left: Cannot go in a command (the name holds a control character, an invisible or direction-changing character, or a wildcard): {left}. Disable them in wf.msc (Inbound Rules, the rule, Disable Rule).
lan_fw_win_noallow: No Windows Firewall rule allows incoming connections to TCP port {port}, so a phone cannot connect. A port rule survives node upgrades, which a program rule does not. In an elevated PowerShell: {command}
lan_fw_win_public: Windows calls the network of {where} Public, which blocks incoming connections: Settings, Network & internet, Wi-Fi, the network, Network profile type, Private.
lan_fw_win_unknown: Windows Firewall could not be read ({why}). If a phone cannot connect, allow the port in an elevated PowerShell with {allow} and list rules that block node.exe with {list}; disable one by its InstanceID with Disable-NetFirewallRule -Name '<InstanceID>'.
